script.opening_words: Picture this. You're 43-years old. It's a Tuesday night, the kids are finally in bed, and you do something you've been quietly avoiding for about 6 months. You log into your retirement account, you stare at the number, and then you just sit there. Because the number on your screen, the sum total of everything you put away for the future after two decades of working, is roughly what a decent used Honda Accord costs. And the worst part isn't
script.ending_words: of them will make a good Instagram post. You're not going to go viral for checking your beneficiary designations or bumping your 401k contribution by 1%, but in 25 years when the second version of you is sitting across from the first version, the one who meant to, but didn't, you'll know exactly which decisions made the difference. Make them now while the math still gives you a fighting chance.
script.analysis: Full 19986 canonical characters read. Persona-driven milestone checklist ("Dave", 43, $95K): retirement benchmark (Fidelity 3x/6x, SCF medians), compounding penalty for delay, retirement income projection, debt hierarchy (cards, cars, student loans), estate planning (wills, beneficiaries), term life insurance, retirement before college (529-to-Roth), mortgage payoff vs invest, 401(k) limits and catch-up, allocation drift, two-Daves ending. Correct: Fidelity multiples, $1,234/$381 monthly, beneficiary rules, 10% penalty, 529 rollover, inflation erosion. Errors: SCF 35-44 median ($60K vs ~$45K), car $1.09M (should be ~$2.09M), $100K at 8% = $1.74M (actually ~$1.01M; uses 10%), apples-to-oranges mortgage comparison, catch-up $730K (~$188K), 2025 limits stale for 2026. Stored ending complete.
